text:
incident-bot: Synthetic monitor alert: /v1/complete in ap-south-1 failing health checks (4 failures in last 7m). Auto-page triggered. :rotating_light:

Marie Chen: I see the bot. Any sign of user-visible errors? Alerts from real traffic?

Priya Nair: Checking realtime metrics now. Client-side 5xx is flat, request rate steady. No active customer tickets in Zendesk. This smells like monitor sensitivity to ephemeral network hiccups.

Rajesh Patel: We rolled a kernel security patch in ap-south-1 ~40m ago. Some nodes showed short-lived DROP connections during reprobes. If probes run at 45s interval and page on 3 fails, that will definitely flare.

Dana Ortiz: Right—we've seen similar with earlier rollouts. Current probe config: interval 45s, fail_threshold 3, timeout 6s. That's aggressive for a region doing rolling kernel restarts.

Marie Chen: Proposed quick mitigation: suppress immediate paging and throttle alerts to the synth-monitoring channel while we confirm infra state. Then increase fail threshold and add longer sustained-fail gating for paging.

eng-sre-bot: Suggested action: add 10m mute for paging -> #synth-monitors, adjust probe -> interval 180s, fail_threshold 5, page_after_sustained 8m. Create follow-up ticket for permanent changes.

Alex Kim: I can push a temp config to probes-cluster. Recommend also enabling randomized jitter so probes aren't synchronized with rollout waves.

Rajesh Patel: Here's the patch I propose we apply immediately (YAML snippet):

```
# temporary probe policy for /v1/complete - ap-south-1
- id: complete-ap-south-1
  interval_seconds: 180
  consecutive_failures: 5
  page_on_sustained_minutes: 8
  jitter: true
  request:
    method: POST
    path: /v1/complete
    body: {"prompt":"ping"}
    timeout_seconds: 7
```

Marie Chen: That looks good. Please don't mute alerts entirely; route them to #synth-monitors and keep a bypass so we can escalate if the monitor detects a clear SLA breach.

Priya Nair: I'll reroute pages and add a temporary subscription so primary on-call isn't paged. Also adding a watch to the incident workspace for the next 6 hours.

eng-sre-bot: Config deploy queued: probes-service v3.5.1 -> prod (canary by zone).

Dana Ortiz: For transparency, I'm posting the host rollout timeline from infra: https://redwood.infra/status/rollouts/2026-03-15 (note: internal link). Kernel patch completed in ap-south-1 at 40m ago; some nodes finished at 25m ago.

Alex Kim: Rolling patch to probes now. Applying to staging canary then to ap-south-1.

eng-sre-bot: Deploy started. Monitoring canary for 3 minutes before region rollout.

Marie Chen: While the change is in flight, please start a short correlational dashboard so we can see probe failures vs pod restarts and ephemeral network errors. I don't want to chase false positives later.

Rajesh Patel: I'll create a Grafana panel with three series: probe_fail_rate (1m), pod_restart_count (5m), and tcp_reset_rate (1m). Link will be added to the follow-up.

Alex Kim: Staging sanity: with new settings, probe failures dropped to single sporadic blips, no sustained alarms. Proceeding to region rollout.

eng-sre-bot: Deploy completed to ap-south-1 (canary success). No immediate errors.

Marie Chen: Recording customer impact check: No Intercom or Zendesk tickets, no increased error budget consumption. Marking customer-impact: none at this time.

Dana Ortiz: Follow-up Jira created: INF-5210 "synth-probe-hysteresis-and-dashboard" assigned to eng-sre, priority P2. Tasks:
- Long-term probe hysteresis design (exponential backoff + region dampening)
- Dashboard correlating probes and real traffic
- Add probe-failure simulation test in CI (simulate transient TCP resets)
- Add runbook entry for temporary probe relax during infra maintenance

Marie Chen: For the next on-call handoff: Priya will own monitoring for 12 hours; escalate to Rajesh if sustained failures reappear. Priya, please add notes to the handoff doc.

Priya Nair: Ack. I'll put a note in the oncall doc and keep the watch channel open.

Rajesh Patel: Small automation I want added to INF-5210: if kernel patch rollout is detected (via infra API), automatically increase probe interval and escalate a notification to synth-monitoring channel. That should prevent human-in-the-loop to reduce pages during known maintenance.

Dana Ortiz: Good idea. Also adding a unit test requirement: any probe that runs against public-facing endpoints must have a flakiness budget recorded and use adaptive thresholds if above X% historical volatility.

Marie Chen: One more ops detail: adding a tiny helper script to quickly rollback the probe policy if needed. Alex, can you commit this to infra-tools?

Alex Kim: Pushing script now:
```
#!/bin/bash
set -e
kubectl apply -f /manifests/probes/complete-ap-south-1-patch.yaml -n probes
sleep 30
curl -fsS https://probes-service.internal/health || { echo "probes-service unhealthy"; exit 2; }
# verify no sustained fails in 10m window
```

Marie Chen: Thanks. Any objections to keeping this thread open for 6 hours then closing if no regression?

eng-sre-bot: Triage update: probe policy adjusted, pages routed to #synth-monitors, follow-up INF-5210 created. Monitoring window: 6h.

Priya Nair: No objections. I'll post periodic status updates in #synth-monitors and close the watch after 6 hours if stable.

Rajesh Patel: For INF-5210 backlog items, I'll include docs for when to apply temporary relaxations vs when to treat probe failure as true incident. We need clearer decision criteria.

Marie Chen: Great. Thanks everyone. Closing this thread unless someone reports a new event. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Thread closed by Marie Chen. Summary: synthetic monitor flapping during infra kernel rollout in ap-south-1; temporary probe hysteresis applied and paging suppressed to synth-monitoring channel; INF-5210 created for longer-term mitigations and dashboards.
